text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel wants the government to decide on NATO membership by the end of the year. However, the Social Democrats, senior coalition partners, want to adhere to the planned date of 1998.
- Agricultural group Raiffeisen and milk producers NOeM and Bergland are having talks over the possibility of joining forces to become more competitive.

- New immigration laws presented by the government yesterday are planned to help integrate foreigners living in Austria legally better, while clamping down on immigration. Opposition parties criticise the draft law as either too soft or too hard.
- Multinational food corporations starting business in eastern Europe are continuing to maintain production locations in Austria.
- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner plans to go ahead with reforming Austria's trade regulations even if farmers do not agree to participate.

- French salt producer Compagnie des Salins du Midi, a subsidiary of U.S. salt and chemicals giant Morton, has guaranteed jobs will not be lost if its offer for Austria's salt-monopoly Salinen AG is accepted.
- Petrol prices in Austria will rise in 1998 if the European Union goes ahead with its planned taxation of resources.
- Orders at Jenbacher Energiesysteme have more than tripled to 342 million schillings in January and February this year compared to the previous year.
DIE PRESSE
- Parliament will decide on a reform of the law on working hours next week.
- Austrian Airlines are believed to be paying 500 to 700 million schillings for the 36 percent stake in rival Lauda Air.
- Austria's federal union demands employment should become the sixth convergence criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union.
- The reform of apprentice education has not brought the expected rise in apprentice jobs.
- Austria is losing ground in eastern European markets, as it faces growing problems with investment and stagnating exports.
KURIER
- Austrian Airlines' takeover of Lauda Air should strengthen the country's airlines. The price for the 36-percent-stake is expected to be about 150 million schillings.
- Central bank chief Klaus Liebscher demands banks must reduce fees for investors to secure the future of the Vienna stock exchange.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Special investment funds are intended to reduce the risk for investors in the stock exchange's new "fit"-programme for small and medium-sized companies.
